docs.title: Memory
docs.text: types of Memory: 1.Stack: Stores temporary variables and separate memory block for methods Stores primitive data types stores reference of heap objects each thread has its own stack memory variables within a scope is only visible and as soon any variables goes out of scope it gets deleted from the stack(LIFO order) new() -creates memory in heap and refernce in stack(there are 3 type of reference(Strong,weak and soft)) String is stored in string pool inside heap garbage collector is used to delete unreferenced object from the heap Strong Reference: Person p=new Person(); WeaK Reference : if gc runs it will be freed Soft reference : do it when if urgent need of memory is required 2.heap Memory : Contains two generation : 1.young generation 2.old generation 1.young generation consists of eden and survior space when obj is created it goes to eden Survivor Space: This contains the objects that have survived from the Young garbage collection or Minor garbage collection. We have two equally divided survivor spaces called S0 and S1. once GC runs it removes unreferenced objects and move others to survivor and age the object Once threshold age is met it moves to older generation Meta space : Class variable(static) metadata ,constant are stored in this.

docs.title: Functional Interface
docs.text:
If an interface contains only 1 Abstract method for ex: public inteface bird{ void canFly(string val); } --only 1 abstract method it can have default,static or method inherited from the object class

A method reference is the simplified syntax used for a lambda expression that executes just ONE method.

Sometimes, the lambda expression is just a call to one method, for example:

Consumer<String> c = s -> System.out.println(s); To make the code more simple, you can turn that lambda expression into a method reference:

Consumer<String> c = System.out::println;

docs.title: Lifecycle of a Spring Bean
docs.text:
1. Application Start

    • Spring application starts, initializing the runtime environment.

  2. IOC Container Initialization

    • Spring IoC container starts.
    • Configuration metadata is loaded (XML, annotations, or Java config).

  3. Bean Instantiation

    • Container creates an instance of the bean using its constructor.

  4. Dependency Injection

    • Dependencies are injected into the bean.
    • @Autowired is used to inject other beans by type.

  5. @PostConstruct Method Execution

    • Runs after dependencies are injected and before the bean is used.
    • Used for initialization tasks.

  6. Bean Usage

    • Bean is ready to be used by the application.

  7. @PreDestroy Method Execution

    • Runs before the bean is destroyed.
    • Used to clean up resources like closing DB connections.

  8. Bean Destruction

    • Container removes the bean from memory.

docs.title: Depenedency Injection
docs.text:
Using Dependency injection,we can make our class indepdent of it dependencies It helps to remove the dependency on concrete implementation and inject the dependencies from external source.

Types of Injection: 1. field injection: 1. dependency is set into fields of class directly. 2. Very simple and easy to use 3. Can not be used with immutable fields like final 4. changes of null pointer exception 2. Setter Injection 1.Dependency is set into the fields using the setter method 2. We have to annotate the method using @Autowired public void setorderDependency(Order order){ this.order=order; } Difficult to read and maintained.as per standard,object should be initilized durinh object creation . so this might create code readbility issue.

  1. Constructor Injection
  2. Dependency get resolved at the time of initialization of the object itself. public class user{ Order order; @Autowired public User(Order order){ this.order=order; System.out.println(""); } }
  3. When more than 1 constructor is present,then using @Autowired on constructor is mandatory

docs.title: why constructor injection is recommended(Advantages)
docs.text: All mandatory dependencies are created at initliazation itself.to avoid NPE runtime and unnecessary null can be avoided to. we can create immutable object using constructor injection Fail fast :if there is any missing dependency , it will fail during compilation itself,rather than failing run time.

docs.title: Common issue with dependency injection:
docs.text: -Circular dependency : 1. we should refractor the code and remove the cycle dependency ,remove code to separate class 2. using @lazy on autowired annotation:Spring will create proxy bean instead of instance of bean 3. using @PostConstruct - Unsatisfied dependency : 1. @Primary is an annotation that marks a bean as the default choice when multiple candidates are available for autowiring. It helps Spring avoid confusion when it encounters more than one bean of the same type 2. @Qualifier :When you have multiple beans of the same type, Spring gets confused during autowiring. @Qualifier helps resolve this ambiguity by specifying which bean to inject. @Component("fooFormatter")

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
@Component("fooFormatter")
   public class FooFormatter implements Formatter {
       public String format() {
           return "foo";
       }
   }

@Component("barFormatter")
public class BarFormatter implements Formatter {
    public String format() {
        return "bar";
    }
}
@Autowired
@Qualifier("fooFormatter")
private Formatter formatter; // ✅ Spring injects FooFormatter

docs.title: Aspect Orientated Programming
docs.text:
-In simple term,it helps to intercept the method invocation and we can perform some task before and after method -Allows us to focus on buisness logic and it takes care of boilerplate and reptitive code like logging,transaction management etcs. -help in reusability and maintainbility of code org.springframework.boot spring-boot-starter-aop

@Component @Aspect public class LoggingAspect{ @before("execution(public String com.concept.learningspringboot.Employee.fetchEmployee())") public void beforeMethod{

} } Before and method together is called Advice and Before(") is called pointcut Pointcut:Its an epressin ,which tells where an advice should be applied. Types of PointCut: 1. Execution :matches a particular method in a particular class @before("execution( com.employee.fetchEmployee))-match any return type @before("execution( com.employee.*(String)))- match any method with single parameter string (..) wildcard :match 0 or more item 2. within : mention all method within any class and package @Before("within(com.code.springboot.Employee)") 3. @within :matches any method in a class which has annotation @Before("@within(org.springframework.stereotype.Service)) 4. @annotation: matches any method that is associated with annotation @Before("@annotation(org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping)") 5. Args: matches any method with particular arguments(or parameter) @Before(args(String,int)") 6.@args: matches any method with particular parameters and that parameter class with particular annotation @Before("@args(org.springframework.stereotype.Service)") 7. Target: matches any method on a particular instance of class @Before("target(com.code.learningspringboot.EmployeeUtil)") 8. Named pointcut :

docs.title: JPA
docs.text:
• Java Persistence API is a specification that lets you do Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) over a relational database.

  • ORM allows you to map the entity classes to your relational SQL database.

  • What is Spring Data JPA?

  • Spring Framework handles ORM in an easy and quick fashion using JPA. [Application Logic] ↕ ↕ [JPA] (interface) ↕ ↕ [Hibernate] (implementation) ↕ ↕ [JDBC] (interface) ↕ ↕ [Specific DB Driver] (implementation) ↕ ↕ [Relational DB]

Pom needed to add for JPA Using JDBC with Springboot 

<groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupIp<
<artifactId>spring-boot-starter-jdbc</artifactId>
</dependency>
<dependency>
<groupId>com.h2database</groupId>
<artifactId>h2</artifactIp<
<scope>runtime</scope>
</dependency>
  • Springboot provides JdbcTemplate class, which helps to remove all the boiler code. Driver class loading - JdbcTemplate load it at the time of application startup in DriverManager class. DB Connection Making - jdbcTemplate takes care of it, whenever we execute any query. Exception Handlingin Plain JDBC, we get very abstracted 'SQLException' but in jdbcTemplate, we get granular error like DuplicateKeyException, QueryTimeoutException etc.. (defined in org.springframework.dao package). Closing of the DB connection and other resources - when we invoke update or query method, after success or failure of the operation, jdbcTemplate takes care of either closing or return the connection to Pool itself. Manual handling of DB Connection Pool - Springboot provides default jdbc connection pool i.e. 'HikariCP' with Min and Max pool size of 10. And we can change the configuration in 'application.properties' spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=10 spring.datasource.hikari.minimum-idle=5

docs.title: JPA Architecture
docs.text:
1. peristance unit :Logical grouping of Entity classes which share same configurations.db connect and driver etcs and it used to create EntityManagerFactory
  2. EntityManagerFactory:
  3. Using Persistence Unit configuration, EntityManagerFactory object get created during application startup.
  4. If any property is not provided, default one is picked and set.
  5. 1 EntityManagerFactory for 1 Persistence Unit.
  6. This class act as a Factory to create an object of EntityManager.
  7. Entity Manager and Peristance Context Its an interface in JPA that provides methods to perform CRUD operations on entities. persist() (for saving) merge() (for updating) find() (for fetching) remove() (for deleting) createQuery() (for executing JPQL queries)
  8. EntityManager interface methods are implemented by JPA Vendors like Hibernate etc.
  9. EntityManagerFactory helps to create an Object of EntityManager. PersistenceContext: Consider its a first level cache.
  10. For each EntityManager, PersistenceContext object is created, which hold list of Entities its working on. Also manage the life cycle of entity.

docs.title: Second level caching
docs.text:
need dependency: ehcache,hibernate,javax.cache - In entity we need to add cache annotation - In cache we need region Helps in logical grouping of cached data. For each Region (or say group), we can apply different caching strategy like Eviction policy TTL Cache size Concurrency strategy etc. @Cache (usage = CacheConcurrencyStrategy.READ_WRITE,region = "userDetailsCache") - CacheConcurrencyStrategy - READ_ONLY: Good for Static Data Which do not require any updates - If try to update just entity, exception will come -READ_WRITE:During Read, it put Shared Lock, other Read can also acquire Shared Lock. But no Write operation. During Update, it put Exclusive Lock, other Read and Write operation not allowed. - NONSTRICT_READ_WRITE:During Read, No Lock is acquired at all. During Update, after txn commit successful, Cache is mark Invalidated and not updated with Fresh data. Good for Heavy Read application. - So if Update and Read happens in parallel, its a chance that read operation get the stale data. -Transactional

  • spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto configuration tells hibernate regarding how to create and manage the DB Schema. Mapping classes to table :@Table annotation . it is optional field otherwise entity will name table via enity name @Table(name= "USER_DETAILS", schema= "ONBOARDING")
@Table(name= "USER_DETAILS",
@Entity
})
schema= "ONBOARDING",
uniqueConstraints={
@UniqueConstraint(columnNames="phone"), //single column unique constraint
@UniqueConstraint(columnNames={"name","email"}) //composite unique constraint
  • @columns annotation : Its an Optional field, if not defined, JPA will add it with default values.
  • @Id Annotation and @GeneratedValue Annotation Primary Key: must be unique, not null and used to uniquely identify each record.
  • @Id annotation is used to mark the field as primary key. Each entity can have only 1 primary key. Only 1 field can be annotated with @ld.
  • Composite primary uses @emdebble

docs.title: How to start
docs.text:
Here are the steps to build a simple Spring boot application.

Generate a quick Java project with Maven command.

Update pom.xml with the Spring web and other Spring boot dependencies.

Add SpringApplication.run() method to bootstrap Spring application.

Do a Maven clean build using mvn clean package command.

Execute command mvn spring-boot:run to run the application.

docs.title: SQL Databases - Integration
docs.text:
Spring Boot Framework is quite flexible while working with SQL database. You can use direct JDBC calls using JDBC templates, or you can go by implementing hibernate.

One more significant option that Spring framework offers is by creating repositories for Spring Data implementation.

docs.title: security
docs.text:
Spring Security can be broadly classified as

Authentication

Authorization

Spring Security architecture distinguishes both authentication and authorization.

Authentication

The interface defined for Authentication is Authentication Manager. This is a single method Interface.

public interface AuthenticationManager { Authentication authenticate(Authentication authentication) throws AuthenticationException; }
